leak: Every part of the system identified a game as 'Away@Home'. A doubleheader puts two games on that one name, so game 2's starters, prices and flag silently overwrote game 1's - the site showed the same matchup twice with identical data, and the nightly grader would have scored the game-2 play against game 1's final score.
ev: Caught live by a subscriber on the Cardinals-Reds twin bill. The 9:00 AM lineup lock texted a Cardinals play for GAME 1 (10:40 AM) - but the text carried game 2's starters and price, and the site showed both games as the same -116 official play. Subscribers bet game 1; the Cardinals won 2-1. During the repair the not-yet-played game 2 briefly graded as a WIN off game 1's final, and a stray 'no bet, game already started' note went out for the finished game 1 - both symptoms of one name covering two games.
fix: Games now carry their MLB game ID and game number end to end. Doubleheader game 2 gets its own key everywhere (lineups, prices, plays, texts, the paper F5 ledger, the board), and any row that knows its game ID grades ONLY against that game - no fallback that a twin's score could leak through. The record: game 1 IS the texted play (win, at the texted -116); game 2 was never texted and is not a play. Subscribers were sent a clarification.

leak: Plays were firing in matchups where a starting pitcher had almost no season data, forcing the model to lean on career stats.
ev: Bets trusting OUR OWN thin-sample starter: 11-22, -$759. Bets fading a thin starter: 16-13, +$269. Thin starters with elite swing-and-miss (11%+ whiff): their teams win 55% - the market knows the returning ace better than a career-stat blend does.
fix: Side-aware gate: the starter behind our bet needs ~50+ innings; thin opponents are fadeable only when their stuff is unproven. We fade call-ups, never returning aces.

leak: CLV was graded against 'closing' odds pulled at 10:30 PM - which, for finished games, could be the NEXT day's lines for the same teams.
ev: Rebuilt against true pre-pitch snapshots (545 games): the flattering +2.65% average CLV was really +0.77% on all picks. But flagged plays held up: +6.49%, beating the true close 96% of the time.
fix: Every graded game re-scored against the actual line 10 minutes before its first pitch; closing lines now date-filtered permanently.

leak: The odds feed returns several days of games. Prices were keyed by team name only, so tomorrow's line could silently overwrite today's - producing phantom edges and wrong prices in alerts.
ev: Caught live: one game showed a 90-cent spread across books (two different games mixed); one play fired on next-day prices and would not have qualified at the real ones.
fix: Every price consumer filters to the exact slate date before reading a single number.

leak: A play could be texted at 2 PM, then a later pre-game re-run would re-price the game and silently drop or change the flag - so the record graded something different than what subscribers bet.
ev: Caught when a texted -105 play vanished from the nightly grade; the day was reported 1-1 when the truth was 1-2.
fix: Lock-on-text: the moment a play is texted, its price and flag are frozen. The texted price IS the official play, forever.

leak: When the value was on the underdog, the graders scored the bet as if it were on the favorite - value-dog wins were recorded as losses for months.
ev: 13 bets graded on the wrong team. Corrected season P&L swung from -$1,425 to -$152 - over $1,200 of losses never happened.
fix: One shared source of truth for which side carries every bet, used by every grader, notifier, and report. Covered by regression tests.

leak: The old pipeline bet its biggest edges hardest - and they were its worst bets.
ev: Edges of 10%+ claimed 58.9% confidence and cashed 44.6%. The 3-6% zone claimed 52.7% and cashed 61.8%. Moderate disagreement with the market is signal; huge disagreement is usually our error.
fix: The 3-8% bet window: bets live where the model has been right, capped before the zone where the market is.

leak: On every game with confirmed lineups, the old inference code fed each team's offense into the model under the OTHER team's label - flipping the sign of the second-strongest feature.
ev: Re-scoring 117 live games: the raw model picked at 58.1% while the full buggy pipeline delivered 53.9%.
fix: V2 rebuilt with one shared feature module for training and inference - the same definition, mathematically incapable of drifting apart.

leak: After the model produced a calibrated probability, four hand-tuned adjustments (park factor, home boost, bullpen nudge, probability clamp) 'improved' it.
ev: The layers flipped 28% of picks; the raw model won 57.6% of those disagreements. The clamp alone discarded the model's most confident - and most accurate - calls.
fix: All four layers deleted. Park and bullpen numbers are still shown as context; they just don't touch the number.

leak: The weekly retrain silently excluded the current season from training - 757 of the freshest games taught the model nothing, all season.
ev: The 'current season weighted 3x' log line printed every week; the rows it referenced were never in the training set.
fix: Trains on everything, validated by walk-forward so no holdout season is needed for an honest number.

leak: The old model used 18 inputs. Permutation testing showed 13 of them made out-of-sample predictions WORSE - extra dimensions the model used to memorize the past.
ev: Only the pitching gap carried clearly positive signal. Walk-forward: the 4-feature rebuild beat the 18-feature original 60.2% to 58.7%.
fix: Four winsorized features into a calibrated logistic regression. Any new feature must beat this baseline out-of-sample before earning a slot - tested, never assumed.

leak: The old pipeline kept betting into games where professional money had moved the line against it.
ev: Those bets went 2-15 (13.3%) for -$1,062 before the veto existed. Sharps opposing the model win ~58% of the time.
fix: The FADE veto: any play with significant sharp movement against it is killed automatically, no exceptions.
